summary: The recorded base deterministically reproduced the false host-memory rejection, while the exact candidate passed the same contract and independent allocator, page-size, parsing, non-additivity, and multi-rank boundary cases. No source-level counterexample remains for the original preflight-accounting bug.

tests.what_was_measured: Actual imported base host_memory_budget_bytes returned 2 GiB and rejected a 7 GiB request despite a simulated matching 12 GiB free hugetlb pool; see base-contract.txt.
The exact candidate's imported source returned the matching 12 GiB hugetlb budget and admitted the original 7 GiB request; see candidate-contract.txt.
Candidate regression suite: 8 passed, covering the reported case and its committed boundaries; see candidate-focused-retry.txt.

Independent cases verified alternative pools are not added, the larger pool wins, hugetlb capacity is rank-split, mismatched/malformed meminfo is rejected, and only the eligible default allocator uses recognized hugepage settings; see candidate-adversarial.txt.

gpu_execution_evidence: One AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950 device was detected with Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2, but the reviewed change is CPU host-memory accounting and no GPU numerical claim was made.
remaining_limitations: The review host has HugePages_Total=0, so a physical hugetlb-backed mmap and the reporter's full server/model startup were not reproduced; changing node-wide hugepage reservations was outside scope.
No model weights were needed or used. This review does not qualify model semantics, HTTP serving, or multi-node behavior.
